title: About
content:
Stock Anatomy takes products apart and finds the listed Korean companies that make each component.

When a new smartphone, robot, electric car or weapon system comes out, most coverage stops at the brand on the box. We go one layer down: which parts are inside, and which companies listed on the Korean stock market (KOSPI and KOSDAQ) actually make them.

What we publish

  • Teardowns: one product per post, broken down part by part, with the listed maker of each part where it can be confirmed.
  • Supply-chain notes: how much a single product can mean for a Korean supplier, using figures from filings, company announcements and published reports.

How we decide whether to name a company

We only name a supplier when there is evidence. Every company we mention carries one of these four labels:

LabelWhen we use it
FilingThe customer or supplier appears in an official filing, such as a Korean DART business report or a U.S. SEC filing.
AnnouncedThe part maker or the product maker has announced the relationship itself (press release, trade show, official statement).
ReportedA news outlet has reported it. We always name the outlet and link the article.
EstimatedNo evidence of the three kinds above. We say it is an estimate and we do not name the company.

If a supplier we listed as estimated is later confirmed, we update the post, change the label and refresh the "last checked" date at the bottom.

About the images and videos

Our teardown images and videos are reconstructions made from public information, not photographs of a physical disassembly. Each post says so under the images.
